scope: finite isotropic log-concave cone counterexample only; no KLS conclusion
independent_reproduction: Integrating (1/2)e^{-s} over |y|<=s gives s e^{-s}, which integrates to 1. S is Gamma(2,1): E[S]=2 and Var(S)=2. Given S=s, Y is uniform[-s,s], so E[Y]=E[SY]=0 and E[Y^2]=E[S^2]/3=2. Therefore X=(S-2)/sqrt(2), Z=Y/sqrt(2) have mean zero and covariance I. The affine Jacobian is 2; p_{X,Z}(x,z)=e^{-(2+sqrt(2)x)} on x>=-sqrt(2), |z|<=x+sqrt(2). Convex support and affine log-density prove log-concavity. For a=x+sqrt(2)>0, Z|X=x is uniform[-a,a]; using g(z)=z in Var(g)<=C_P E|g'|^2 gives C_P>=a^2/3. For any M>0, a^2/3>M on S>sqrt(6M), whose Gamma(2,1) tail is (1+sqrt(6M))e^{-sqrt(6M)}>0.
source_quote: Testing the conditional Poincare inequality on g(z)=z shows C_P(law(Z|X=x)) >= a^2/3.
remaining_gap: No general KLS bound or smooth uniformly convex variant follows from this finite counterexample.

scope: failure of the stated conditional-derivative identity for this law and f(x,z)=z^2
independent_reproduction: For a=x+sqrt(2)>0, E[z^2|X=x]=(1/(2a))*integral_{-a}^a z^2 dz=a^2/3; differentiation gives 2a/3. Since partial_x(z^2)=0 at fixed z, E[partial_x f|X=x]=0. The two sides differ for every interior x.
source_quote: Its conditional mean is m(x)=a^2/3 and m'(x)=2a/3, whereas E[partial_x f(X,Z)|X=x]=0.
remaining_gap: A valid conditional argument may include a derivative-of-law or boundary term; this verdict addresses only the stated identity.
